#comment1: TEST CONFIG, not a production alignment. Question: do stave-level DOFs alone build the IB/OB direction kink seen in checkResid (dPar2 = IB-OB snp at 12 cm, n=2 vs phi: 73 urad in V10n, ~175 urad in v8..v18)?
#comment2: In v18 - V10n the kink is carried entirely by translations of the IB half barrels/staves (-2..-3.4 um r*dphi ~cos2phi) and of the OB staves (Lr3,4 -6..-7 um, Lr6 +7 um); modules, chips and sensor rotations contribute < 0.3 um.
#comment3: So everything below the staves is fixed, and so are the stave rotations (they only give z-odd terms). Run it on the same V10n-based Mille data as v8..v18 and compare dPar2 vs phi (and the per-layer n=2 r*dphi vs V10n) with v18.
#comment4: Gauge as in v19: no rdphi ray cells (they pinned the OB rotation relative to IB+vertex); the whole-ray r*dphi rotation is pinned on the IB only (tangentialHarmonic), curl by the ITS RZ pin. dz/dr ray cells kept OB-only but with nT=1, since stave DOFs at z~0 cannot realise a t dependence (16 t cells would be redundant equations).

#comment: OB half barrels stay fixed; with only the staves free below them the mean-of-staves pin catches any net half-barrel motion, so the v18 globalShift groupModes (needed against the module-level scissor) would duplicate it
same stave TX prior as v18, for comparability
whole-ray rotation r*dphi = eps*r*cos/sin(l*phi), l=1..4, pinned on the IB only: the OB rotation relative to IB+vertex is left to the tracks
v18 OB global modes reachable by stave translations (twist and the t-odd polar members need z-distributed DOFs or RY, which are fixed here)
